title: Local Tor bounds pass to affine module models
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open of S, W an open containing U, and K in D(\mathcal O_S) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let P be a complex of modules over R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S) whose termwise affine associated sheaf complex represents K restricted to U, through [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model]. If the derived restriction of K to W [def-pc-derived-pullback] has finite Tor dimension [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension], then Q(P) has Tor amplitude in some finite interval: for every R-module N its derived tensor with N[0] has cohomology only in that interval.

source.place: Tags 08CG, 08E9(1), 08DX(2), and 09U8, affine restriction of a Tor interval

proof.text: Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.TorAmplitudeOpenLocal and reuse its existing private helpers AlgebraicGeometry.exists_kFlat_model and AlgebraicGeometry.open_pullback_model_iso, rather than declaring either statement again. They supply a K-flat representative C of K and the comparison of derived pullback along W.ι with termwise exact restriction. Transport the latter along the representing isomorphism eC and mapDerivedCategoryFactors to identify (derivedPullback W.ι)(K) with RW.mapDerivedCategory(K). Write j = isoSpec.inv followed by S.homOfLE hUW. Restriction composition and S.homOfLE_ι identify RW followed by restriction along j with restriction to U followed by overEquiv and restriction along isoSpec.inv.

Apply exact derived-functor composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons to the preceding functor isomorphism. Apply the representing isomorphism hP. Cancel overEquiv.inverse followed by overEquiv.functor with its counit, then cancel isoSpec.hom and isoSpec.inv with restriction composition and the inverse identity. Map the resulting affine sheafification cancellation isomorphism to complexes and apply Q. This constructs an isomorphism between the restriction along j of (derivedPullback W.ι)(K) and Q(tilde(P)).

Unpack the interval a ≤ b and universal tensor vanishing on W. For every module sheaf G on Spec Gamma(U,O) and degree i outside the interval, apply the single-degree open-immersion vanishing test along j to the hypothesis tested on j_*G. Transport the K-flat witness through the representing isomorphism of step 2. This gives the sheaf-side premise of affine_torAmplitude_iff. Its forward implication yields the required module Tor amplitude, with the same a and b.
